task.description:
Implement the design at lib/letflow/design/iss0451-poller-crash-budget-isolation.md exactly as specified (it passed CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's gate after 2 rework cycles, both of which found and fixed real OTP-semantics defects -- the design has been independently re-verified live, twice, so implement it as written rather than second-guessing its mechanism choices; if you find a genuine additional defect while implementing, stop and report it rather than silently deviating).

Summary of what the design requires (read the design doc itself for the authoritative, complete spec -- this is a pointer, not a restatement):
1. A new module Letflow.Supervisor.PollersBreaker (circuit breaker GenServer) at lib/letflow/supervisor/pollers_breaker.ex, per the design's state machine (:closed/:open/:half_open), monitoring Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers, trip threshold, exponential backoff schedule, and Supervisor.start_child/2-based restart mechanism (NOT restart_child/2 -- the design explicitly corrected this).
2. lib/letflow/application.ex's children list: Pollers' entry changed to Supervisor.child_spec(Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers, restart: :temporary) used directly as the list entry, PollersBreaker added as a new child listed after Pollers and before Http, and the top-level Supervisor.start_link/2 opts' max_restarts raised per the design's stated value.
3. test/letflow/supervisor/pollers_test.exs's existing restart_pollers!/0 helper (or whatever the design calls it) needs updating from terminate_child+restart_child to terminate_child+start_child/2 with the full child spec, per the design's own §5/§6 discussion of this consequence -- this is a required correction to EXISTING test code, not new test authoring (TEST-DESIGNER handles the NEW persistent-fault regression test at the next step; you fix this specific existing-test breakage since it's a structural consequence of your own application.ex/pollers.ex changes, not new coverage).

After implementing: run `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` and `mix format --check-formatted` and fix anything either flags. Run the EXISTING test/letflow/supervisor/ test files (pollers_test.exs, infrastructure_test.exs, http_test.exs) and confirm they still pass under your changes -- REQ-219's own AC2/AC4 tests living in pollers_test.exs must not regress (per ISS-0451's own AC3). Do NOT write the new persistent-fault regression test yourself -- that is TEST-DESIGNER's job at the next step; you may leave a TODO comment or simply leave it to that step.

This will then go to SECURITY-REVIEWER (supervision-tree/boot-sequence changes are in scope even though this isn't a tenant-data path -- confirm scope test yourself and state your reasoning either way) and REVIEWER (OTP idiom, supervision integrity) before TEST-DESIGNER.
acceptance_criteria: lib/letflow/supervisor/pollers_breaker.ex created, matching the design's module/state/callback spec
lib/letflow/application.ex updated per the design (child spec syntax, PollersBreaker added, max_restarts value)
test/letflow/supervisor/pollers_test.exs's restart helper corrected to use start_child/2, not restart_child/2, per the design's own required consequence
test/letflow/supervisor/pollers_test.exs, infrastructure_test.exs, http_test.exs all still pass (REQ-219 AC2/AC4 no regression, per ISS-0451 AC3)
No new persistent-fault regression test written by this step -- that is TEST-DESIGNER's job next
task.rework_note: REWORK ITERATION 1 (of your own Step 3 -- this reuses the same handoff file rather than opening a new step number since it's the same task, now unblocked). CODE-DESIGNER resolved the race you found (result.issues[0] on this handoff, from your own prior attempt) by rewriting lib/letflow/design/iss0451-poller-crash-budget-isolation.md's section 5 -- CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR independently re-verified the fix and PASSED it (handoffs/WF03-ISS0451-20260904/step-02b-code-design-validator.json, gate_history[3]). The chosen fix is option 2 of your own three named directions: the AC4 test no longer issues its own competing Supervisor.start_child/2 call at all. Read the CURRENT section 5 in the design doc (it has been rewritten, do not rely on your memory of the old version that caused the FAIL) -- it now specifies: trigger with terminate_child/2 alone, then poll PollersBreaker.breaker_state()/Process.whereis/1 until a new Pollers pid appears while breaker_state() == :closed (proving the single-shot fault never tripped the breaker), then the original Repo/Infrastructure pid-unchanged assertions, plus one new assertion (breaker_state() == :closed). Your own production code (lib/letflow/supervisor/pollers_breaker.ex, lib/letflow/application.ex) needs NO further changes -- both CODE-DESIGNER and CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR independently confirmed this (git diff between the two design revisions touched only the .md file). Apply the new section 5 procedure to test/letflow/supervisor/pollers_test.exs's AC4 test (replacing your own prior implementation of the old, broken guidance), then re-run test/letflow/supervisor/pollers_test.exs, infrastructure_test.exs, and http_test.exs to confirm all pass reliably (run pollers_test.exs multiple times with varied --seed, the way you did before, to confirm the flakiness is actually gone this time -- don't assume it from the design doc alone). Finish this handoff normally per HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 4 (status COMPLETED, full result block, completed_at from the real clock) -- if it now passes cleanly, route to SECURITY-REVIEWER next as the original task described.

gate_history.summary: Production code (pollers_breaker.ex, application.ex) implemented correctly per the then-current design, compiled and formatted clean. But applying design section 5's THEN-guidance to pollers_test.exs's existing AC4 test surfaced a genuine, previously-unflagged race: PollersBreaker and the test process both react to the same terminate_child-induced :DOWN and race to restart Pollers -- reproduced deterministically at seed 0, flaky (2/5) otherwise.
issues: BLOCKER: two-restarter race in the AC4 test's adaptation, full detail retained in git history of this file (commit at 2026-09-04T03:30:42Z) -- routed to CODE-DESIGNER, resolved via a redesigned section 5 (single breaker-mediated flow, no test-issued competing start_child/2 call), independently re-verified PASS by CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR.
